newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly down on Tuesday on overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at 22,990 yuan ($2,772) per tonne, losing 70 yuan.
It opened at 23,000 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,050 yuan and a low of 22,910 yuan per tonne.
July fell 90 to 22,530, August 90 to 22,670, September 20 to 22,870, November 30 to 23,050 and December 60 to 23,040 yuan.
Combined volume fell to 50,380 tonnes from 82,200 tonnes.
Copper opened lower and fell further before short-covering pushed prices from intraday lows late in the session.
Traders said substantial selling continued to pour into the market in the morning session, with market sentiment further dampened by the LME losses.
LME three months copper ended Monday's afternoon kerb $56 weaker at $2,511 per tonne, despite a late rebound that pared early losses.
Traders in London said the red metal faced resistance at $2,500, and was vulnerable to test support around $2,465.
"Investor confidence seemed unable to recover due to Monday's fresh LME falls until some speculative buying emerged late in the session," one Shanghai trader said.
"But volume dropped against Monday, indicating initiative selling is slowly grinding to a halt," he added.
Physical prices were lower around 22,600 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area due to falls on the futures market.
Traders said late-maturing contracts continued to find support at the 23,000 yuan level but further direction would depend on copper's performance on the LME.
"Shanghai copper will not be able to stand above the 23,000 yuan level if the LME continues this downtrend trend over the next few days," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended down. July fell 150 to 13,900, August 240 to 13,910 and September 210 to 14,100 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 1,050 tonnes from 2,000 tonnes.
